plan_summary: Give the terminal failure-reason vocabulary an explicit retriable/non-retriable severity split, sourced from the classification execution-report.js already computes. Three files change, all inside policy.allowed_paths. (1) adws-pipeline/references/phase-gates.md replaces the prose 'Failure-reason classes' bullet lists with ONE authoritative table that defines every terminal reason and states its severity in the same row, adds two new NON-RETRIABLE reasons — ADVOCATE_DISSENT_UPHELD (an operator-upheld Advocate dissent) and EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH (a skill_trace verdict that disagrees with its own validator output, or evidence present-but-unreadable) — and states the sourcing rule: the severity column is the projection of execution-report.js's NO_RETRY_REASONS/QUARANTINE_REASONS sets, read by the orchestrator from the report's own decision/exit_code (or the new exported classifier), NEVER re-derived by parsing gates[].detail prose. (2) adws-pipeline/references/artifact-layout.md pins run_manifest.failure_reason to that closed vocabulary, separates it from attempt-level annotations, and names EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH at the skill_trace transcription rule that already describes the breach. (3) adws-pipeline/scripts/execution-report.js adds the two new reasons to the existing sets (ADVOCATE_DISSENT_UPHELD to NO_RETRY_REASONS beside ADVOCATE_DISSENT; EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH to BOTH sets, mirroring MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT exactly) and adds ONE derived, exported classifier — failureReasonSeverity(reason) -> 'retriable' | 'non-retriable' | null — computed from those same two sets and CALLED by decideLifecycle's 'failed' branch, so there is exactly one severity computation in the toolchain rather than a doc list that can drift from the code. Deliberate non-changes, each load-bearing: DECISIONS, GATE_STATUSES, exit codes, gate keys and the emitted execution_report.{json,md} shape are all untouched, and SCHEMA_VERSION stays '1.4.0' because parity/execution-report-fixtures/run-tests.js hard-asserts that literal and parity/ is a blocked path; PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED and STABILITY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED are documented as terminally RETRIABLE and must NOT be added to either code set, since adding them would silently redefine an existing reason's verdict. adws-pipeline/SKILL.md is not in allowed_paths and needs no edit: its 'Failure-reason classes' section already delegates authority to references/phase-gates.md and its gate rule already says {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE is the default 'unless a more specific reason applies'.

file_change_proposal.description: The authoritative change. Replace the 'Failure-reason classes (port of phases.js reason sets)' section (currently two prose bullet lists, no severity per reason) with a single definition TABLE whose columns are: Reason | Emitted when | In-run: skips remaining retry budget? | Terminal severity (retriable = RETRY / non-retriable = QUARANTINE) | Source set in execution-report.js. Rows cover the whole closed enum: CREDENTIAL_FAILURE, OPERATOR_CANCEL, MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT, PLAN_COHERENCE_BELOW_THRESHOLD (reserved), ADVOCATE_DISSENT (unresolved dissent — meaning unchanged), the new ADVOCATE_DISSENT_UPHELD, the new EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH, PR_DRIFT_SENTINEL_BLOCK, PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED, STABILITY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, and {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE with its concrete expansions. Every row states its severity in that same row, so severity is never a separate list that can drift (AC-1). Keep the in-run 'no-retry' notion and the terminal severity as SEPARATE columns: PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED is no-retry in-run but terminally RETRIABLE, and flattening the two would silently redefine it. Directly under the table add the sourcing paragraph (AC-4): the severity column is the documented projection of NO_RETRY_REASONS and QUARANTINE_REASONS in scripts/execution-report.js; a run's severity is read from the report's own decision/exit_code (QUARANTINE/2 = non-retriable, RETRY/1 = retriable) or from the exported failureReasonSeverity() classifier, and is NEVER re-derived by parsing gates[].detail or any other gate prose. Add a short adjacent note listing the ATTEMPT-level annotations (ADVOCATE_DISSENT_REPAIRED, CRITIC_FAIL_REPAIRED) that are not terminal reasons, carry no severity, and never reach decideLifecycle. Then update the three sites that currently route an upheld dissent or an integrity breach into the blanket reason: Consensus rule 5's `action: "uphold"` bullet (today 'QUARANTINE / ADVOCATE_DISSENT') now names the distinct terminal reason ADVOCATE_DISSENT_UPHELD and says explicitly it is NOT {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE (AC-2); 'Operator-directed repair of a correct dissent' step 5 (where a spent repair cap leaves override or uphold) names the same reason; and Gate rules (imperative) rule 5 is amended so the default {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE applies only when no more-specific row of the table applies, with the evidence-integrity case named — a terminal skills_clean gate failure on its integrity terms (trace/output disagreement on any attempt, latest or superseded, or an evidence file present but unreadable/malformed) terminates on EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH (AC-3). Update the Contents list entry 'Failure-reason classes — no-retry vs quarantine-class' to match the new section title.

Make the evidence-schema side agree with the new vocabulary without duplicating it. (a) In the run_manifest.json prose (the paragraph that today only says final_status is null while running and set once at terminal state), state that failure_reason is likewise null while running and set once at terminal state to a value from the CLOSED vocabulary table in references/phase-gates.md, and that its retriable/non-retriable severity is read from that table — which is the projection of execution-report.js's own reason sets — never re-derived by a reader parsing report prose (supports AC-1 and AC-4). (b) In the phase_manifest.json prose, distinguish the ATTEMPT-level failure_reason, which may carry annotations like ADVOCATE_DISSENT_REPAIRED and CRITIC_FAIL_REPAIRED that have no terminal severity, from run_manifest.failure_reason, which must be a terminal-vocabulary value. (c) In the skill_trace 'The wrapper is a transcription, never a judgment (SC-8/F-55)' paragraph, which already says a disagreement 'quarantines the job — an evidence-integrity breach, the same class as MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT', name the reason it now terminates on: EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH (non-retriable), same class as MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT and no longer collapsed into {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE (AC-3). All three are cross-references and clarifications; no reason is defined or given a severity here, so the table stays the single definition site.

Make the code carry the severity the docs project, additively. (1) Add 'ADVOCATE_DISSENT_UPHELD' to NO_RETRY_REASONS (lines 53-59) beside ADVOCATE_DISSENT, so an upheld dissent recorded in run_manifest.failure_reason maps to QUARANTINE instead of falling through decideLifecycle's default to RETRY (AC-2). (2) Add 'EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH' to BOTH NO_RETRY_REASONS and QUARANTINE_REASONS (line 61), mirroring MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT exactly, which is the class the file's own SC-8/F-55 and SC-11/F-69 comments already assign to this breach (AC-3). (3) Add the derived, exported classifier immediately below those sets — a frozen SEVERITIES constant ('retriable' | 'non-retriable') and failureReasonSeverity(reason) returning null for a null/non-string/empty reason, 'non-retriable' when NO_RETRY_REASONS.has(reason) || QUARANTINE_REASONS.has(reason), and 'retriable' otherwise. It must be COMPUTED from those two sets, never a third hand-maintained list, so the classification cannot fork. (4) Rewire decideLifecycle's `failed` branch (lines 899-921) to compute `const severity = failureReasonSeverity(reason)` once and branch on it, keeping QUARANTINE_REASONS.has(reason) solely to choose between the two existing decision_reason wordings — every returned decision, warn_flag, decision_reason string and exit code stays byte-identical for every reason that exists today, which is what keeps the parity fixture corpus scoring the same decision and exit code. (5) Export SEVERITIES and failureReasonSeverity from module.exports beside the already-exported NO_RETRY_REASONS/QUARANTINE_REASONS, so the severity is machine-readable at a named seam rather than inferred from prose (AC-4). (6) Extend the header comment block that records additive changes with a note on this change. Explicit non-changes the builder must honor: do NOT bump SCHEMA_VERSION (parity/execution-report-fixtures/run-tests.js asserts the literal '1.4.0' and parity/ is a blocked path), do NOT alter the emitted report object's keys, gate keys, DECISIONS, GATE_STATUSES or exitCodeFor, and do NOT add PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED or STABILITY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED to either set — both are terminally retriable by design and adding them would change an existing reason's verdict.

criteria_map.criterion: The terminal failure reason vocabulary documents, for every reason, whether that reason is retriable or non-retriable, and the severity is stated in the same table the reason is defined in.
criteria_map.check_idea: Parse the single vocabulary table out of adws-pipeline/references/phase-gates.md and assert (a) it exists as one markdown table with a terminal-severity column, (b) every row's severity cell is exactly 'retriable' or 'non-retriable' (no blanks, no free text), and (c) every terminal reason token used anywhere in adws-pipeline/ (regex [A-Z][A-Z_]{3,} plus the {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE family, minus an explicit allowlist of the attempt-level annotations ADVOCATE_DISSENT_REPAIRED and CRITIC_FAIL_REPAIRED) appears as a row of that table. Falsifiable baseline: on the pre-change tree the section is two prose bullet lists with no table and no per-reason severity, so the check is RED because the feature is absent, not because it cannot run.

criteria_map.criterion: An upheld advocate dissent terminates on a distinct non-retriable failure reason rather than on the blanket phase gate failure reason.
criteria_map.check_idea: Two joined assertions. Code: node -e requiring adws-pipeline/scripts/execution-report.js asserts NO_RETRY_REASONS.has('ADVOCATE_DISSENT_UPHELD'), failureReasonSeverity('ADVOCATE_DISSENT_UPHELD') === 'non-retriable', and decideLifecycle({ status: 'failed', failureReason: 'ADVOCATE_DISSENT_UPHELD', gates: [] }).decision === 'QUARANTINE' — while decideLifecycle for 'REVIEW_GATE_FAILURE' still returns 'RETRY', proving the two are distinct reasons with distinct severities. Docs: the phase-gates Consensus `uphold` bullet names ADVOCATE_DISSENT_UPHELD and the table row for it reads non-retriable, and ADVOCATE_DISSENT (unresolved) keeps its own row and its existing meaning. Falsifiable baseline: pre-change the string does not exist, so decideLifecycle returns RETRY for it (unknown reason -> retriable) and the check goes RED for the right reason.

criteria_map.criterion: An evidence integrity breach terminates on a distinct non-retriable failure reason rather than on the blanket phase gate failure reason.
criteria_map.check_idea: node -e asserts NO_RETRY_REASONS.has('EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH') && QUARANTINE_REASONS.has('EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH') (same membership as MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT), failureReasonSeverity('EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH') === 'non-retriable', and decideLifecycle({ status: 'failed', failureReason: 'EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH', gates: [] }) returns decision 'QUARANTINE' with the quarantine-class decision_reason wording. Docs side: grep that phase-gates.md's gate-rule-5 text and table route a skills_clean integrity failure (trace/output disagreement, or present-but-unreadable evidence) to EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH rather than {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE, and that artifact-layout.md's skill_trace transcription rule names the same reason. Falsifiable baseline: pre-change the reason is absent from both sets and decideLifecycle maps it to RETRY.

criteria_map.criterion: The severity of a terminal failure reason is sourced from the classification execution-report.js already computes, not re-derived by an orchestrator parsing gate detail strings.
criteria_map.check_idea: Drift check that joins the doc table to the code sets: read every (reason, severity) pair out of the phase-gates table (expanding {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE to the seven concrete phase names), require the exported failureReasonSeverity(reason) to equal the table's severity for EVERY row, and require decideLifecycle({ status: 'failed', failureReason: reason, gates: [] }).decision to be 'QUARANTINE' exactly when that severity is 'non-retriable' and 'RETRY' otherwise — so the documented column is provably a projection of the one classification the script computes rather than independent prose. Add the converse direction too: every member of NO_RETRY_REASONS union QUARANTINE_REASONS must appear in the table as non-retriable, so the code cannot gain a reason the table omits. Falsifiable baseline: pre-change there is no severity column and no exported classifier, so the check cannot find the pairs and goes RED for the right reason. Regression guard for constraint 4 (run, never modify — parity/ is a blocked path): node parity/execution-report-fixtures/run-tests.js and node parity/run-parity.js must both still pass with every fixture's decision and exit code unchanged, which also pins SCHEMA_VERSION at '1.4.0' and the emitted report shape.
